items.title: app/embed/[id]: no postMessage events to the host page (connected, trade confirmed, market resolved)
items.description: **Context**: The embed widget (`src/app/embed/[id]/page.tsx`) is a black box to the site embedding it. **Problem**: The README pitches embeddability as a distribution channel, but a host site can't measure conversions, show its own confirmation, or react to resolution. Without events there's no way to tell whether embeds drive any trading — the number that says the embed strategy works. **Proposed change**: Emit a small documented set of `postMessage` events (`polaris:ready`, `polaris:connected`, `polaris:trade` with `{side, txHash}`, `polaris:resolved`) with `targetOrigin '*'` and no addresses or amounts. **Acceptance criteria**: - [ ] Events fire at the stated moments; payload schema documented in the embed guide - [ ] No wallet address, balance, or position size in any payload

items.title: app/embed/[id]: fixed 360×420 iframe with no height auto-resize — content clips or leaves dead space
items.description: **Context**: `EmbedCodeButton` hands out a fixed `width="360" height="420"` snippet. The widget's content height varies: the email fallback form (`AuthControls compact`), a `ResultReveal` with "Next round is live", or a multi-line error all change it. **Problem**: Taller states get an internal scrollbar or clipped buttons inside the host page; shorter ones leave a blank box. Hosts have no way to know the right height. (#50/#66 cover query-param customization, not dynamic sizing.) **Proposed change**: Post `{ type: 'polaris:resize', height }` to `window.parent` from a `ResizeObserver` on the widget root, and include a 5-line listener in the generated snippet. **Acceptance criteria**: - [ ] Widget posts its height on mount and on every size change - [ ] Snippet with the listener resizes the iframe across all widget states - [ ] Message carries no wallet or position data

items.title: Remove the activity record from the core; forward migration drops ledger and recorded-session tables
items.description: ### Goal The core no longer keeps an activity record. The ledger, the recorded sessions and the read API for them are removed; a forward migration drops their tables. What the core keeps is the chat session history for resuming, which is deleted with its session or server as before. Session activity is only available to extensions through the observer hook from #1505. ### Context - Decided by maintainer: there is no activity record in the core; existing ledger data is discarded (it was never shown anywhere in the app). - Record tables: `ledger_entries` (since `0011`, rebuilt in `0029_activity_record.sql`), `activity_sessions` and the column `chat_sessions.activity_session_id` (`0029`, no foreign key on that column). - Code: `crates/persistence-sqlite/src/{ledger_store.rs, activity_session_store.rs, record_query.rs}`, `crates/app-logic/src/record_query.rs`, `crates/app-logic/src/ext.rs:110-140` (record read functions), `crates/app-shell/src/commands/record.rs`, record functions in `apps/smart-ssh-community/frontend/src/public-api.ts` and `api/`, the funnel `write_ledger_entry` (`crates/app-logic/src/orchestration/chat_turn.rs:230`) and its call sites, `crates/core/src/audit/`, `AppState.ledger_store` / `activity_session_store`, `session_builder.rs:468-470`. - Docs: Spec 0057, ADR 0047, ADR 0160, recipe `docs/recipes/extension-reads-activity-record.md`, THREAT-MODEL.md sections on the record, Spec 0038 (record commands). - Migration pitfall: sqlx runs a migration in a transaction where `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` has no effect; never rebuild `chat_sessions` (dropping it would cascade into `chat_messages`). ### Requirements - Migration `0030_remove_activity_record.sql`: `DROP TABLE ledger_entries;` then `DROP TABLE activity_sessions;` then `ALTER TABLE chat_sessions DROP COLUMN activity_session_id;` (plain column, no index, no FK). items.title: Queue menu Clamp current song to top or bottom when scrolling far ahead or behind
items.description: I get lost really easily in my super long liked shuffle queue because theres no way to tell if I'm too far up or too far down. I suggest clamping the current song to within the screen bounds (image 2 and 3) so that even when far away I know which direction to scroll to get back to the current place in the queue. The current song highlight box maybe should be a full bar instead of an inset rounded rectangle so that the shape merges with the bottom or top section. Apple music's solution is History and Continue playing as different categories (image 3 and 4), its a different design choice entirely but still helps know where the user is. Also, I suggest cutting the scroll velocity when the current song reaches the default position, that way you don't have to time perfectly when scrolling fast. Maybe the cut only happens if the current song is being clamped (so not already within screen bounds) when the user scrolls to avoid cutting when the user *wants* to scroll away. Also also, I suggest adding a small header to the top of the screen. My phone overlaps the top bar with the songs, its not ideal. It'd be the same accent color as the bottom panel for consistency and so that the highlight song merges with the top cleanly too. The list button currently at the bottom could be moved up there (along with the song counter next to it) since that button opens a drop-down at the top of the screen anyway. samsung a53 **Attachments** ![Screenshot_20261104_124005_InterTune.jpg](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1567597102236966942/1567597102421508147/Screenshot_20261104_124005_InterTune.jpg?ex=6b047d11&is=6b032b91&hm=94ce5b4074a66b0e06c5bccf68c4354a6b84a0af2cafd454420881e2e60efd27&) ![Screenshot_20261104_124027_InterTune.jpg](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1567597102236966942/1567597102970966117/Screenshot_20261104_124027_InterTune.jpg?ex=6b047d11&is=6b032b91&hm=0659831cc73d65f6f340b009cfdb2a6888cf351047c89ad3d391bbff0c409cd4&) ![Screenshot_20261104_124149_Apple_Music.jpg](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1567597102236966942/1567597103457509546/Screenshot_20261104_124149_Apple_Music.jpg?ex=6b047d12&is=6b032b92&hm=b5e161079a5f4fa6171e5e20a0241408f1f7f1122892e42aa034eb9bbe8b125f&) ![Screenshot_20261104_124219_Apple_Music.jpg](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1567597102236966942/1567597103985860659/Screenshot_20261104_124219_Apple_Music.jpg?ex=6b047d12&is=6b032b92&hm=193e835562361c36423770cffc27f7f9ec5f593a47503931fa21043aefa2a7ac&) _Images are re-sig

items.title: Semanais: escolher o vídeo da semana por flag (LinkedIn + Stack); re-seleção do pós-gate apaga o override
items.description: ## Evidência (pacote semanal 26w47, 21/11/2026) O editor pediu, no gate, para trocar o vídeo da semana pelo "Claude Code pode ter vazado suas senhas no GitHub" (edição 261112, semana anterior), no LinkedIn e na Stack. O vídeo automático era o mais visto da janela (`resolveTopEditionVideo`, #12081), "Google te dá Gemini 4 Hydrogen de graça" (261116). Não existe flag para escolher o vídeo. Para fazer a troca: - editei à mão o campo `video` de `data/weekly/26w47/_internal/ln-selection.json` e de `circle-stack-selection.json` (título, URL, `editionDate`); - `select-linkedin-weekly.ts --shared-selection ... --require-approved` (Passo 7 do pacote) **reescreveu `ln-selection.json` sem o campo `video`**, e o render seguinte voltaria a buscar o mais visto. Precisei salvar e restaurar o campo antes de renderizar. ## Fazer - Flag `--video-edition AAMMDD` (ou `--video-url`) em `select-linkedin-weekly.ts`, `render-linkedin-weekly.ts` e `publish-circle-stack.ts`, que resolve título e URL pelo `_internal/05-youtube-published.json` da edição, aceitando edição de fora da janela. - Override gravado de forma que a re-seleção do pós-gate (`--require-approved`) preserve. - No `/diaria-pacote-semanal`: uma troca só que vale para LinkedIn e Stack, e invalida a frase do vídeo (#13045) e a descrição do vídeo da Stack, que precisam ser reescritas. ## Prioridade P2: a troca é um pedido editorial que já aconteceu, e o caminho manual perde o override em silêncio no pós-gate. Sem o restauro, o artigo sairia com o vídeo errado.

items.title: Make ShareX cross-platform with a platform abstraction layer (Windows, macOS, Linux)
items.description: ## Summary Make **every part of ShareX** run natively on Windows, macOS and Linux, including major distributions (Ubuntu/Debian, Fedora/RHEL, Arch-based such as Omarchy, EndeavourOS, Manjaro, and openSUSE). This covers the whole product, not only capture and upload: the main application UI, the image editor, image effects, screen recording, history, tools, destinations/uploaders, settings and the setup/packaging pipeline. Development branch: `cross-platform-v2` (branched from `develop` after the SkiaSharp/Avalonia migration). The earlier `cross-platform` branch is frozen at `55e0c7d90` and no longer receives work. ## Scope In scope (all must work on all three OSes, with no feature that is Windows-only by design): - **Main application** (`ShareX`): main window, tray, hotkeys, workflows, task manager, settings, history, after-capture pipeline. - **Image editor** (`ShareX.ImageEditor`, `ShareX.ImageEditor.App`): editor core, canvas, annotation tools, effects, standalone app and embedded use from the main app. - **Capture** (`ShareX.ScreenCaptureLib`): region, window, full screen, scrolling capture, screen recording, OCR. - **Image effects** (`ShareX.ImageEffectsLib`), **tools** (`ShareX.Tools`), **history** (`ShareX.HistoryLib`), **destinations/uploaders** (`ShareX.Destinations`, `ShareX.UploadersLib`), **helpers** (`ShareX.HelpersLib`). - **Browser integration** (`ShareX.NativeMessagingHost`) and **packaging/setup** (`ShareX.Setup`). Out of scope only when an OS has no equivalent and the feature degrades with a clear, user-facing reason and install hint (for example Explorer-specific shell integration on macOS). ## Goals - Platform-agnostic interfaces (e.g. `IPlatformServices`) with implementations in `ShareX.Platform.Windows`, `ShareX.Platform.MacOS`, `ShareX.Platform.Linux`. - Move Win32/P/Invoke usage behind these interfaces. - Migrate the UI from WinForms to a cross-platform toolkit (Avalonia, `ShareX.Avalonia`) so the main app and image editor share one UI codebase. - Keep Windows behaviour unchanged. ## Areas to abstract - **Screen capture**: GDI/DWM, ScreenCaptureKit/CoreGraphics, X11 and Wayland (xdg-desktop-portal/PipeWire). - **Screen recording**: FFmpeg per OS (gdigrab/ddagrab, avfoundation, x11grab/pipewire). - **Global hotkeys**: RegisterHotKey, CGEventTap, XGrabKey, Wayland GlobalShortcuts portal. - **Clipboard**: Win32, NSPasteboard, X11/Wayland (wl-clipboard fallback). - **Tray and notifications**: NotifyIcon, NSStatusItem, StatusNotifierItem

items.title: idea: one cast reference per outfit - wardrobe variants so a costume change holds the face (OpenMontage)
items.description: **Source.** charliewwdev/OpenMontage ("Drama Studio", read 2026-11-22). Its licence is AGPL-3.0, so this is concepts only: no code is taken. **What it is.** Their character bible (`schemas/artifacts/character_bible.schema.json`) gives each character a list of `wardrobe_variants`, each with its own `id`, `label`, `description` and `reference_images`. A shot names a character plus the outfit, and that outfit's references go to the generator. Our cast sheet (#1400) and series procedure (`dw:series-episodes`) hold **one look per character**. **Why it may matter for us.** Our own bench (`plugins/dw/skills/minimax-h3/references/cuts.md`, *the card holds what it shows*) found that a whole-clip reference lost the wardrobe colour, and that wardrobe holds only through the window or "by putting it in the portrait". A series or scene with a costume change therefore needs a portrait (or cast sheet) for each outfit. The skills don't say this yet, and the requests ledger has no way to name which outfit a shot used. **Candidate shape (for the lead to change or drop):** 1. Skill text in `dw:series-episodes` / `dw:storyboard` / `dw:script-to-video`: cast once per character **and outfit**, from the same face (draw each outfit from the first portrait so the face holds), and name the outfit in each shot's item note. 2. A probe that answers whether the outfit portraits keep the face: SFace / face_drift across outfits of one character, against a single-portrait control. **Open questions.** Can the outfit stills be made on FLUX 3 Klein (multi-reference edit from the base portrait) so that mini-ai can run the whole probe? H3 clips on mini-ai take about 9 min each and only load from lem's pre-quantized folders. If the probe needs H3 clips, the lead may want to move the clip arm to lem. Does a face-once cast sheet (#1400) already cover this if the neck-down views are redrawn per outfit? **Ask.** Owner lead: evaluate whether this is worth a plan, and either write one (with probes and cost) or close it with the reason. Target mini-ai where the work allows it. (recorded by claude-opus-5-5 via anthropic in Don's session)

items.title: CI gives its result fast and cheap, and keeps the Mac usable
items.description: ## Problem A PR's CI takes tens of minutes, and it runs on the development Mac. Three self-hosted runners each keep their own checkout and Rust target, about 9 GiB each, and compile Rust, C and Lean at full priority. Tonight the load average reached 190 on 12 cores, and the Mac was close to unusable while CI ran. ## Why this matters The language owner's goals, in order: CI is faster, uses less memory, and uses less CPU, and the Mac stays usable while CI runs. CI only targets the machines PHP# is built and run on: this Mac (arm64 macOS), Linux VMs, the Hetzner machines (x86_64 Ubuntu 24.04) and the devbox. PHP# supports no other platform, compiler or configuration, so a check for one is deleted. ## Agent Brief **Category:** enhancement **Summary:** a PR's CI gives its result fast, cheap and off the Mac's foreground, without hiding a single failure **Two rules outrank speed:** - **The full suite runs before anything reaches `master`.** A batch PR's merge runs the whole suite on the head it merges. Running only what a change can reach narrows feedback on a builder's push, and never the merge. - **Never get faster by hiding failures.** No retries, no wider timeouts, no skipped tests. A check that needs a retry has a bug, so find it. **First, audit.** Pull the last 150 runs of every workflow and split every job into waiting, setup and running, at p50 and p95. Post the table on this issue. Fix the biggest bucket first. It's rarely the tests, so don't start by deleting them. **Targets,** each measured from real runs, before and after: - **Result:** a builder's push gets its result in under 5 minutes at the median and under 8 at p95. The full suite on a merge stays under 15 minutes. - **The Mac:** a CI job on the Mac runs at background priority (`taskpolicy -b`, or `nice -n 20` plus a core cap) and never on more than half the cores. With CI running, the load average stays under 12 and memory pressure stays green. - **CPU and memory:** total CPU-seconds per run and peak RSS per job both go down, and the post shows them. **Decided design:** - **Jobs that need no Mac leave the Mac.** Everything but the macOS build, its tests and the macOS release asset runs on Linux. Where it runs, on GitHub's hosted runners or on the language owner's Hetzner machines, is decided by the audit's waiting numbers. A runner on a machine needs a registration token, so bring that as a list. - **Build caches are allowed in CI.** The no-cache rule is about `mago`'s own speed, not about CI. C

items.title: Document step edits files outside a run's declared narrow scope
items.description: When a run is meant to change only a few files, the Document step still edits documentation elsewhere in the repository, and nothing at its gate shows that it did. We hit this four times in one day, on four independent tasks, each followed by a manual scope review before the change could ship. Version: `no-mistakes v1.106.1 (5732d1e)`. This build already includes #1638, the fix for #1557, which tells both Document passes to respect the intent's file restrictions and to park an off-limits repair as `ask-user`. ## What happens 1. Each run was submitted with an explicit `--intent` describing a narrow change (for example, one config file, or one instruction file). The intent described what to change. The file limit itself ("change only this file", "this plan is immutable") was stated in the instructions to the agent that submitted the run, and was not repeated in the intent as a file restriction. 2. The Document step found a fact the change touched, located its "authoritative owner document" elsewhere in the repository, and edited that file. 3. The edit was committed as a `no-mistakes(document): ...` commit. The step reported no finding, so its gate did not park. 4. The candidate's diff was now wider than its declared scope. A reviewer had to notice that, then decide whether to keep or revert the document commit. The four tasks were unrelated: an approval change, a networking change, an instruction-file change, and a one-file runbook fix. ## Why it happens In `internal/pipeline/steps/document.go`, the task text tells the agent to find each altered fact's owner document wherever it lives and fix it there. The step computes `git diff --name-only base..head`, but only to decide whether to run at all. The agent never receives that file list as a boundary, and after the agent runs, `commitAgentFixesWithResult` commits whatever it edited. The gate parks only if the agent itself reports a finding (`NeedsApproval: len(docFindings.Items) > 0`). So the only protection is the `documentScopeDiscipline` sentence "Respect the run's intent restrictions on files". That works only when the intent spells out a file restriction. In our runs it described the change instead, so the Document agent had no visible boundary, and "fix the owner document" won. The `intentConformanceReviewClause` that turns an explicit intent into an `ask-user` obligation is wired into Review, not Document. items.title: 0.5.0: Add pure random and randomPerFrame (Random surface foundation)
items.description: ## Parent #2 ## What to build Add the foundation of the public Random surface in `komotion-core/.../Random.kt`: four functions that delegate through the internal `seededRandom` factory (issue #5): - `random(seed: String): Double` — pure, returns `Double` in `[0.0, 1.0)`. Same seed → same value, callable from non-Composable contexts. - `random(seed: Long): Double` — same, with `Long` seed. - `@Composable randomPerFrame(seed: String): Double` — reads `LocalFrame.current` and folds it into the seed via `seededRandom(seed, frame = LocalFrame.current).nextDouble()`. Same `(seed, frame)` is reproducible; different frames produce different values for the same seed. - `@Composable randomPerFrame(seed: Long): Double` — same, with `Long` seed. All four are marked `@ExperimentalKomotionApi`. Pure variants are top-level `fun`; `*PerFrame` variants are `@Composable` (visible at the call site that the value is frame-dependent — IDE/compiler enforces "must be inside @Composable"). Seed types are `String` and `Long` only — no `Any?` overload (avoids `toString()` allocation and silent-correctness footguns from `data class` copy semantics). `Random.kt` imports only `seededRandom` from `internal/SeededRandom.kt` — it does **not** import `KotlinRandom`, `fnv1a64`, or `combineHash` directly. The public surface stays a thin delegation layer. Tests in `RandomTest.kt` (using `runComposeUiTest` for the Composable variants) cover: same-seed determinism for both seed types, different-seed distinctness, output range `[0.0, 1.0)` over many seeds, frame-folding produces distinct values, frame-folding is reproducible. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `komotion-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/dev/boling/komotion/core/Random.kt` exists with the four functions above - [ ] All four marked `@ExperimentalKomotionApi`; the two `*PerFrame` variants additionally `@Composable` - [ ] `Random.kt` imports `dev.boling.komotion.core.internal.seededRandom` and nothing from the hashing internals directly - [ ] KDoc on `random(String)` shows a usage example; KDoc on `randomPerFrame` explicitly contrasts it against the pure variant - [ ] `komotion-core/src/commonTest/kotlin/dev/boling/komotion/core/RandomTest.kt` exists with six tests covering String/Long determinism, distinctness across seeds, output range, frame-varying for `*PerFrame`, and `(seed, frame)` reproducibility - [ ] `./gradlew :komotion-core:desktopTest --tests "dev.boling.komotion.core.RandomTest"` passes (6 tests) - [ ] Single commit `feat(core): a

items.title: stair_scum: an exploration mode for characters under 25 max HP (owner proposal, level-1 death review of 206cf4e7)
items.description: Track P. The owner's proposal, from the level-1 death review of track-p `206cf4e7` (borg-zoo run 45070528012, attempt 2): > I would like to have a "stair_scum" setting for low characters: they explore the level in a way that they can go back to the stairs faster than any character can come at them, that is sometimes just two or three steps from the stair, open the doors to check what is there, or at least explore radially, without committing to a direction and then come back and find out they have been cut off. [...] until they have at least 25 HP or so. This is not a tighter leash. It is an exploration **mode**: a radius that depends on how early a monster can be seen, exploration that keeps returning toward the staircase, a peek at every door, and a new level when the safe area is used up. ## Why (the 20 deaths) - **14 of the 20 dead Borgs had max HP under 25**: all 13 at CL ≤ 2, and Mage 584191223 at CL4 with 17 HP. That is the mode's population. - **They died inside today's leash.** C's leash (12 flow steps at CL1, `flow_leash_per_level`/`_base`; return at 17) held in 10 of the 12 CL ≤ 2 monster deaths. The other two went through its holes (#1062). items.title: Ask HN: Are startups today worth it even in a best case scenario?
items.description: I'm gonna open this with the disclaimer that this is purely a financial and risk comparison post. No one is complaining that we are poorly compensated. It is good to discuss compensation so we can make informed and educated decisions when deciding how to commit the next few years of our lives. A close friend of mine joined an AI startup (being intentionally vague) around 1.5 years ago and despite the company doing extremely well on valuation, I'm surprised at how he's not really better off than just working at a large tech company. Concrete numbers for the startup: -200k salary -Equity grant over 4 years is 500k -The company's valuation has since went from single billions to tens of billions, leaving him with a 10x multiplier when looking only at valuation. After you account for dilution, it's closer to 6x. -Liquidity event annually allows you to sell 10% of your vested shares Big tech at a similar years of experience is around 400-500k total comp, and the RSU component is generally liquid. For example sake and ease of calculation, if you assume that my friend's entire equity was vested, and he was able to sell 10% of it, it would amount to approximately $300k/liquidity event, which brings him to around 500k a year as well (200k + 300k). In reality, he's really only able to access $300k/4 since that's all he has vested and that brings him closer to $75k for this liquidity event. There are a lot of variables I'm leaving out obviously such as potential future value, IPO, etc., but the thing that is surprising to me overall is that this is a close to best case outcome, yet the employee doesn't really end up any better off than big tech due to lack of liquidity and dilution. I mean I get it, impact, interesting work, etc. -- the qualitative measures -- aren't really accounted for, but I'm not looking to make a wholistic comparison. This brings me to the question: Is the risk in a startup ever justified for a lower level employee (engineer, Product Manager, Program Manager, etc.)?

items.title: Ask HN: Should Uber Ratings Decay over Time?
items.description: I’ve been thinking about how platforms like Uber calculate reputation scores, and I believe there’s a fundamental flaw in how historical ratings are treated. Uber calculates passenger ratings using the last 500 rated trips, regardless of when those trips occurred. In my case, I have 455 ratings, 426 of which are five stars (93.6%). My overall rating is 4.86. What bothers me isn’t the score itself, but the underlying methodology. A negative rating from five years ago can carry exactly the same weight as one received yesterday. And if you’re an infrequent user who hasn’t accumulated 500 ratings, that negative feedback could influence your reputation for years. This raises an interesting question: Should reputation systems measure your historical average, or should they attempt to represent who you are today? One possible solution is exponential time decay: Weight = 2^(-t/H) Where t is the age of the rating and H is a half-life, perhaps 12 months. Under that approach, a rating from one year ago would carry 50% of its original weight, and one from two years ago just 25%. Of course, this introduces other challenges. How do you prevent someone with a history of poor behaviour from simply waiting for their reputation to recover? How do you maintain statistical confidence for infrequent users? Would Bayesian smoothing or a minimum effective sample size help? There’s also a broader philosophical question around the right to be forgotten. Should digital reputation systems indefinitely preserve the consequences of historical assessments, particularly when those assessments are subjective and potentially no longer representative? I’m curious how others would approach this. * Is a rolling window of 500 ratings statistically defensible without considering time? * Would exponential decay produce a fairer and more predictive reputation score? * Should platforms expose both a lifetime rating and a recent-behaviour rating? * Are there better approaches already being used in other reputation systems? I’d be particularly interested in perspectives from people who’ve worked on marketplace ranking, trust and safety, or reputation algorithms. It seems like a relatively simple mathematical change, but one with potentially significant implications for fairness across digital platforms.

items.title: Ask HN: Do you feel developers are more "grumpy" these days?
items.description: I genuinely am questioning whether this is my perception or it's real. The whole AI coding and threats and opportunities in our industry, makes me think that I might be right, but then again that could be my bias. I wanted to see how everybody else thinks about this. Do you also feel that when you're in a developer-focused subreddit, X communities, or other places, and even on Hacker News, the developers there are harsher in their responses, less friendly, more polarized, and, I would generalize it, grumpier? I remember reading something here a few weeks ago that did a data analysis comparison between Hacker News posts in the past and recent ones, and it sort of said that sentiments have shifted more negative recently. It feels like we all feel threatened by AI, excited by the opportunities, and at the same time, sometimes I feel that as AI has made coding and creation of SaaS companies so competitive that we're also anxious at the same time at the elevated level.
